speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly which antibiotic you were taking and when did the fever, itchy rash, and joint pain start relative to the last dose?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the symptoms improve when you stopped the amoxicillin, and have you noticed any swelling in her face, lips, or difficulty breathing? I also need to check if she has any joint swelling or if the rash is painful to the touch.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor

Given the history of sore throat two weeks ago, followed by low-grade fever, rash, and joint pain, I suspect a post-streptococcal complication. REQUEST TEST: Anti-Streptolysin_O_Titer

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal ASO titer and ESR make rheumatic fever or post-streptococcal reactive arthritis unlikely. Since the rash is non-blanching and she has joint pain, I need to rule out vasculitis. Does the rash have a palpable, purpuric quality, and does she have any abdominal pain or blood in her stool?

speaker: Doctor
text: Does she have any abdominal pain, blood in her stool, or any swelling in her ankles or around her eyes? I also need to confirm if the rash feels raised or "bumpy" to the touch, which would suggest palpable purpura.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal inflammatory markers and lack of abdominal or renal symptoms make IgA vasculitis unlikely despite the rash description. Since the symptoms began one week after starting amoxicillin and involve fever, rash, and joint pain, this presentation is highly consistent with a serum sickness-like reaction. DIAGNOSIS READY: Serum sickness-like reaction
